name: code-for-qs400
description: Develop on QS/400: libraries, source members, the IFS, compiles and debugging, over QAP.
author: Quartz Systems

code-for-qs400.host.path.markdownDescription: Path to a `qs400-code-host` binary. Leave empty to use the one bundled with the extension.

code-for-qs400.connections.markdownDescription: Saved connections. `name` is unique and is the key for the saved password and the library list. Passwords are never kept here: they go to VS Code secret storage. Edit with the **Add Connection** and **Edit Connection** commands, or here.

name.description: Unique connection name, for example QSHQ400.

host.description: Host name or address of the QS/400 system. The server certificate must carry this name.

port.description: QAP port. Leave it out for the default port.

user.description: User profile to sign on as.

verify.markdownDescription: Must be `true`. QAP accepts only a verified server certificate, as QS/400 Access does; to trust a self-signed certificate, name it in `caFile`.

caFile.description: PEM file with certificates to trust beyond the system store: a CA, or the server certificate itself.

libraryList.markdownDescription: Library list applied to the session job on connect. The Library list node edits it.

user.description: User part of the library list, in order.

filters.markdownDescription: Object filters, shown under **Filters** in the Objects view. Edit them with **Add Filter** and **Edit Filter**.

name.description: Filter name, unique within the connection.

object.description: A name, a name ending in * (ASSET*), or *ALL.

type.description: An object type such as *FILE, or *ALL.

attribute.description: An attribute such as PF-SRC or RPGLE. Leave it out for any.

ifsRoots.markdownDescription: Top-level folders of the **IFS** view, in order; the first is Home. Left out: `/home/<user>` and `/`. Edit them with **Add IFS Root**, **Remove IFS Root** and **Set as IFS Home**.

name.markdownDescription: Shown in the action pick. Unique without case: an action of the same name in a workspace folder overrides the default one, and a connection's overrides both.

command.markdownDescription: The CL command. Variables: `&LIBRARY` `&NAME` `&TYPE` `&EXT` `&SRCFILE` `&SRCLIB` `&CURLIB` `&USERNAME` `&HOST` `&FULLPATH` `&PARENT` `&BASENAME` `&BASENAMEEXT` and `&CUSTOM:NAME`; `&&` is a literal `&`. The command's name decides how it runs: a compile the spec lists (`CRTBNDRPG`, `CRTRPGMOD`, `CRTSQLRPGI`, `CRTBNDCL`, `CRTCLMOD`, `CRTPF`, `CRTLF`, `CRTDSPF`, `CRTPRTF`, `CRTCMD`, `RUNSQLSTM`, `CRTPGM`, `CRTSRVPGM`) returns diagnostics for the Problems panel; anything else runs as a command.

enumDescriptions: An object in the Objects view.

extensions.markdownDescription: Member types (`RPGLE`) or file extensions (`rpgle`, `sql`), or object types for `object` (`*PGM`); compared without case. Left out, or `*`: every target of the environment.

enumDescriptions: The member's source file, the file's folder, or the object's type node.
The library the action ran in.
refresh.description: What to refresh in the views after the action ends.

enumDescriptions: In the connection job, waiting for it to end: messages and diagnostics come back.
Submitted with SBMJOB to QBATCH: the job's name comes back, but no diagnostics.

actions.markdownDescription: Actions of this connection, the same shape as `.vscode/actions.json`. One with the name of a workspace or default action overrides it, for a site's `TGTRLS` or `DBGVIEW`.

variables.markdownDescription: Values of `&CUSTOM:NAME` in actions, by name: `{ "TGTRLS": "V1R0M0" }` is `&CUSTOM:TGTRLS`.

code-for-qs400.defaultConnection.markdownDescription: Name of the default connection: offered first when a command asks for a connection, and marked in the Connections view.

code-for-qs400.jobs.autoRefresh.markdownDescription: Refresh the **Jobs** view every 30 seconds while it is shown.

enumDescriptions: A notification for each inquiry that waits for a reply, with Reply and Show.
A notification for every message that arrives on your own queue.
No notifications; the Messages view's badge still counts.
code-for-qs400.messages.notify.markdownDescription: Which messages arriving on your own message queue show a notification. Every arrival counts on the **Messages** view's badge.

scripts.pretest: npm run build && npm run compile-tests && npm run test:grammar
